version.changelog: La skill puente ahora se llama f100k-puente

llm.summary: This skill has a legitimate trend-alert purpose, but its instructions conflict about notification channels and missing-config handling while using local user/business data and external alert tools.

dimensions.detail: The skill is intended for scheduled automation and broad natural-language triggers, and it may read local configuration plus USER.md/cerebro context, use Apify/Tavily/web search, and prepare outbound Telegram or Gmail content containing niche and trend data without a single clear approval flow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains only a Markdown skill file and no executable install scripts, bundled code, dependencies, or static-scan findings.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The artifact gives conflicting directions: OpenClaw-specific text says Phase 5 must not send email and should alert through Telegram, while Phase 5 later instructs Gmail draft creation; it also conflicts on whether to create a missing config from USER.md/cerebro or stop and run another routine.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No system persistence, privilege escalation, backdoors, or destructive actions are present, but the skill can create or rely on persistent local configuration and external notification drafts/messages.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose of detecting emerging trends is coherent with reading niche keywords, searching web/TikTok sources, and generating an alert or short script when a trend is found.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. It appears aimed at legitimate trend monitoring, but you should clarify that OpenClaw never invokes Gmail if Telegram is intended, define exactly what happens when config is missing, and require explicit confirmation before reading USER.md/cerebro or sending/drafting any alert containing niche, keyword, email, or trend data.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: the artifact itself contains the Telegram-vs-Gmail contradiction for trend alerts, creating ambiguity around where user/business data may be sent or drafted.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Partially accepted: trend-related triggers are purpose-related, but they are broad and paired with scheduled execution plus external tools, increasing unintended activation risk.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: the artifact conflicts on missing-config behavior, either creating config from USER.md/cerebro and confirming by Telegram or stopping and instructing another routine.
[SQP-2] expected: Partially accepted: reading niche, keywords, and email is expected for this skill, but the outbound handling and source files should be disclosed more clearly and governed by explicit confirmation.
